interviewcake_second-largest-item-in-bst.incorrectReason: Uses the largest node's parent even when its left subtree contains the true predecessor; when the largest node is the root, it incorrectly returns that root.

notes.correctness: The largest key is the rightmost node. After excluding that key, a nonempty left subtree supplies its immediate predecessor at its own rightmost node. If that subtree is empty, the last ancestor visited on the rightward path is the predecessor. At least two nodes ensure one of these cases exists.

interviewcake_stock-price.incorrectReason: Clamps the profit to zero although exactly one purchase and later sale are required, even in a falling market.

interviewcake_balanced-binary-tree.incorrectReason: Checks the AVL height condition at every node instead of comparing depths of actual leaves; a single long chain has only one leaf and is balanced under this contract.

interviewcake_bst-checker.incorrectReason: Checks only parent-child comparisons, so a descendant can violate an ancestor bound.

interviewcake_bracket-validator.incorrectReason: Treats all opening brackets as interchangeable, accepting crossed or mismatched bracket types.

interviewcake_cafe-order-checker.incorrectReason: Checks only the multiset of served orders and ignores the required order within each source queue.

interviewcake_nth-fibonacci.incorrectReason: Stops one iteration early for n at least two.

interviewcake_delete-node.incorrectReason: Bypasses the successor without copying its value into the target, deleting the wrong logical element.

interviewcake_linked-list-cycles.incorrectReason: Compares values instead of node identities, falsely detecting cycles when different nodes contain the same value.

interviewcake_find-duplicate-files.incorrectReason: Groups files by size alone and therefore reports different sampled contents as duplicates.

interviewcake_find-duplicate-optimize-fo.incorrectReason: Treats a perfectly full value range as overfull, which can select a value occurring only once.
Returns the cycle-entry successor instead of the cycle entry, which need not be a repeated value.

interviewcake_find-rotation-point.incorrectReason: Returns the last index for an unrotated list instead of the required index zero.

interviewcake_graph-coloring.incorrectReason: Assigns colors using degree alone, so adjacent equal-degree vertices receive the same color.

notes.timeComplexity: O(V+E) expected hash-table operations. At a vertex of degree d, at most d colors are forbidden, so at most d+1 palette entries are examined; color-string hashing costs also apply.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(D) stored color entries for maximum degree D, excluding graph and palette inputs.

interviewcake_highest-product-of-3.incorrectReason: Uses only the three largest values, overlooking two negative values whose product can improve the maximum.

notes.explanation: Maintain the three largest values and the two smallest values at distinct scanned positions. Compare the product of the three largest with the product of the largest and two smallest.
notes.correctness: A positive triple product uses either three positive values or two negative values and one positive value. The three largest maximize the first option; the two smallest together with the largest maximize the second. If no positive product exists, any zero gives the optimum zero. Without either possibility, all values are negative or the input has exactly three elements: the three largest maximize the all-negative product, and for exactly three elements both formulas use the only available triple. The tracked extrema preserve repeated values from distinct positions.

interviewcake_queue-two-stacks.incorrectReason: Pops directly from the input stack, yielding last-in-first-out behavior.

interviewcake_shuffle.incorrectReason: Swaps each position with the full array rather than the remaining suffix, producing a biased permutation distribution.

interviewcake_inflight-entertainment.incorrectReason: Inserts the current movie before checking its partner, allowing a single occurrence to be reused.

interviewcake_kth-to-last-node-in-singly.incorrectReason: Returns a copy of the selected node rather than the original node identity.

interviewcake_largest-stack.incorrectReason: Reports the top value as the maximum even when a larger value lies below it.

notes.explanation: Store each pushed value together with the maximum of the stack prefix ending at that entry, using the built-in stack. Pop discards one pair, and GetMax reads the maximum cached with the current top.

interviewcake_coin.incorrectReason: Counts ordered coin sequences instead of unordered combinations.

interviewcake_merge-sorted-arrays.incorrectReason: Removes repeated values from the merged result, violating multiplicity.

interviewcake_merging-ranges.incorrectReason: Reuses original meeting objects and mutates their endpoints instead of returning newly allocated intervals.

interviewcake_mesh-message.incorrectReason: Uses depth-first search and returns the first route found, which need not use the fewest edges.

interviewcake_compress-url-list.incorrectReason: Confuses creation of character nodes with insertion of a complete word, rejecting empty strings and previously existing prefixes as new words.

notes.timeComplexity: O(L) expected amortized time per insertion of a length-L key, using character-edge hash maps and amortized vector growth.

interviewcake_matching-parens.incorrectReason: Returns the first closing parenthesis after the opener, ignoring nested pairs.

notes.explanation: Scan from the designated opener, increasing depth at each opening parenthesis and decreasing it at each closer. Return the first position where depth returns to zero.
notes.correctness: After processing a character, depth equals the number of open parentheses in the scanned substring that have not yet closed. It begins with the designated opener at depth one, and nested pairs cannot return it to zero. Its first return to zero therefore identifies exactly the matching closer.

interviewcake_permutation-palindrome.incorrectReason: Requires every count to be even and rejects valid odd-length palindromes with one odd count.

notes.explanation: Toggle one parity flag for each of the 26 letters while tracking how many flags are odd. A palindrome permutation exists exactly when at most one flag remains odd.

interviewcake_product-of-other-numbers.incorrectReason: Returns only products of preceding values and omits the suffix contribution.

interviewcake_rectangular-love.incorrectReason: Treats touching edges as overlap and returns a noncanonical zero-area rectangle instead of the all-zero sentinel.

interviewcake_recursive-string-permutati.incorrectReason: Removes repeated occurrences of the final character before recursing, losing required multiplicities.

notes.explanation: Recursively permute the prefix without its last character, then insert that removed character at every position of each smaller permutation. An ordered set removes duplicates.
notes.correctness: Deleting one occurrence of the removed last character from any full permutation leaves a permutation of the remaining prefix. Recursion generates that smaller string, and reinserting at every position regenerates the full permutation. Every generated string has exactly the input multiplicities, while the set retains each distinct result once.
notes.walkthrough: For input ac, recursively permute the prefix a, obtaining {a}. Inserting c before a yields ca; inserting it after a yields ac. The ordered set returns {ac,ca}.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n * n! * log(n! + 1)) worst-case character work for n distinct characters, including string copies and ordered-set comparisons; repeated characters can reduce the generated set.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(n * n!) result and intermediate string storage in the distinct-character worst case, plus O(n) recursion depth.

interviewcake_reverse-linked-list.incorrectReason: Allocates a reversed copy and leaves the original list links unchanged, violating the in-place node-identity contract.

interviewcake_reverse-string-in-place.incorrectReason: Leaves the final character outside the reversed range due to an off-by-one exclusive endpoint.

interviewcake_reverse-words.incorrectReason: Reverses the entire character array without restoring the spelling of each word.

interviewcake_simulate-5-sided-die.incorrectReason: Maps seven equiprobable outcomes modulo five without rejection, so two values occur twice as often as the others.

interviewcake_simulate-7-sided-die.incorrectReason: Maps all twenty-five equally likely pairs modulo seven without rejection, producing unequal outcome counts.

interviewcake_temperature-tracker.incorrectReason: Returns the last inserted temperature as the mode rather than a most frequent temperature.

interviewcake_cake-thief.incorrectReason: Uses a descending-capacity 0/1 update, allowing only one item of each type instead of unlimited copies.

interviewcake_find-unique-int-among-dupl.incorrectReason: Uses bitwise OR, which does not cancel paired identifiers as XOR does.

interviewcake_top-scores.incorrectReason: Emits scores in ascending order instead of the required descending order.

interviewcake_which-appears-twice.incorrectReason: Cancels the range zero through n-1 rather than one through n, leaving an extra n contribution.

interviewcake_word-cloud.incorrectReason: Splits internal apostrophes and hyphens instead of retaining them when surrounded by letters.

notes.timeComplexity: O(n) expected time for n text characters, including token hashing and amortized string growth.
